# gnuradio

**Build a radio out of signal-processing blocks instead of hardware**

- **Version recorded:** 3.10.12.0
- **Categories:** `sdr-toolkits`
- **Upstream:** <https://www.gnuradio.org/>

## What it does

A signal-processing framework and a graphical editor for it. You connect blocks -- sources, filters, demodulators, decoders, sinks -- into a flow graph, and it runs as a real-time radio. The blocks are C++ and Python; the editor, GNU Radio Companion, generates a Python program you can read and edit.

## Why you would want it

Every SDR application is a flow graph someone else already drew. This is where you draw your own, and it is the difference between using the modes somebody wrote a program for and demodulating the signal in front of you. It is also the substrate: gr-satellites, gr-air-modes, gr-rds and the SIGINT tooling are all GNU Radio modules, so this is what they load into.

## Before it will work

A radio to feed it -- gr-osmosdr or SoapySDR provide the hardware sources for RTL-SDR, HackRF, Airspy and the rest, and neither is pulled in automatically. Real-time sample rates are CPU work; a wide flow graph on a slow machine underruns rather than slowing down.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`sdr`](../profiles/sdr.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install gnuradio --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `gnuradio`
  - Mint 22.3 is a major release behind at 3.10.9.2 where every other target carries 3.10.12.0 (measured 2026-08-28). That matters more here than elsewhere: out-of-tree modules are compiled against a specific GNU Radio ABI, so a module built for 3.10.12 will not load under 3.10.9. Anything in this catalog that depends on gnuradio inherits that constraint.

## Known problems

Out-of-tree modules are version-locked to the GNU Radio they were compiled against, and a mismatch shows up as a block that will not import rather than as a version error -- this is the single most common GNU Radio problem and it is why SCOPE.md puts third-party modules behind a working source backend and a pin database rather than in 1.0. Flow graphs written for 3.7 or 3.8 need porting for 3.10; the syntax changed and the errors are not obvious.

The GNU Radio project. Mailing list, matrix chat and extensive tutorials linked from the site; the guided tutorials are the right starting point and are better than most software's.
